# Repository map

<!-- Generated by tools/repo_map.py from the code itself. Do not edit by hand: run `python tools/repo_map.py` after changing files; tests/test_repo_map.py fails while this is out of date. -->

What every file is for and how the files connect, read straight from the code: imports, modules loaded by name, the API routes the browser calls and the background jobs those routes start. For **how the system works** step by step see [FLOWCHART.md](../FLOWCHART.md); for **why** it is built this way see [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md).

384 files · 1305 imports · 68 browser → API links · 27 job links · 43 modules loaded by name · 121 API routes · 19 job kinds

**Reading the diagrams:** `A --> B` A imports B · `A -.->|HTTP| B` A calls an API route that B serves · `A ==>|job| B` A starts a background job that B runs · `A -.->|loads| B` A loads B by name (router, job and driver registries) · `A -.->|runs| B` a script runs or installs B · rounded dashed boxes are other areas.

## The whole app at a glance

The areas of the code and how they connect; tests, tools and styles are in the file index. The browser talks to the backend only over HTTP (`/api/...`, one WebSocket for the live scan, Server-Sent Events for the assistant).

## API routes → jobs → engine

Long work never runs inside a request: a route checks its input and submits a job (thick arrow), the job runs in a worker process (`web/jobs.py`) and calls the engine. Routes that answer at once (measuring, status, settings) are in the area diagrams below.
